## Pull request overview

This pull request fixes 26 TypeScript compilation errors in the `packages/core/src/security/` module by addressing four main categories of issues: interface/class name collisions, Zod 4.x API changes, logger signature updates, and environment type guards.

**Changes:**
- Renamed `PluginConfigValidator` interface to `IPluginConfigValidator` to resolve naming conflict with the class of the same name
- Updated Zod error handling from deprecated `.errors` property to `.issues` for Zod 4.x compatibility
- Modified `logger.error()` calls to use the 3-parameter signature `(message, error?, meta?)` instead of the 2-parameter signature
- Changed environment detection from `typeof window` to `typeof (globalThis as any).window` to fix Node.js TypeScript compilation errors
- Fixed test imports, log levels, and test fixture data to match current API requirements

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.

| packages/core/src/security/plugin-config-validator.ts | Updated Zod error handling from `.errors` to `.issues`, added type parameter to ZodError, fixed logger signature, added casting for partial() method |
| packages/core/src/security/plugin-config-validator.test.ts | Fixed relative imports and changed log level from 'silent' to 'error' |
| packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts | Renamed interface from `PluginConfigValidator` to `IPluginConfigValidator` to avoid name collision, added deprecation notice |
</details>

Inconsistent logger.error usage within this file. This call uses the 3-parameter signature with `undefined` as the second parameter, but other calls in the same file (lines 152, 304, 330) use the 2-parameter signature when there's no Error object. For consistency, when logging without an Error object, use the 2-parameter signature: `this.logger.error(error, { plugin: plugin.name, publisherId })` instead of `this.logger.error(error, undefined, { plugin: plugin.name, publisherId })`.
```suggestion
        this.logger.error(error, { plugin: plugin.name, publisherId });
```

The approach using `typeof (globalThis as any).window` is a workaround for TypeScript compilation in Node.js environments. A more idiomatic approach would be to check for Node.js using `typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node !== undefined` (as used in logger.ts:27) rather than checking for the absence of window. This is more explicit about detecting the Node.js environment and avoids the type assertion.
